answer: Reputation is a scarce, unforgeable resource earned by consistently passing originality checks, and the economy spends it to filter out Sybil clusters before they can compound into a majority. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a velvet as the anchor of the cost.
